title: Carry a dissent on the herding mailbox result and transcribe it through the one dissent writer
action: Mirror StopAndAsk's options/leaning trip on the same three surfaces. (1) herding/mailbox.rs render_brief's result-schema block gains a "dissent" object with claim, alternative and severity plus ONE sentence saying when to fill it; move the byte-exact brief pin (render_brief_keeps_the_result_form_block_byte_identical...) with it. The negative pin at mailbox.rs:654-655 currently bans BOTH "bee cells" and the bare substring "dissent" from the rendered brief; the second half pinned decision 6a6b9975's old boundary, which this cell moves. Retarget it red-first: the brief must still never name a bee command, and the dissent FIELD NAME is now expected. (2) MailboxResult gains dissent: Option<MailboxDissent>{claim, alternative, severity}; parse_result_text reads it leniently exactly like options/leaning — absent, wrong-typed, or missing any of the three fields reads as absent, and the severity string is NEVER checked against the closed set here. (3) run.rs result_envelope re-emits `dissent` only when present, so a result carrying none keeps today's exact key set. Then the transcription: where the run verb holds the parsed result and the store root, call the SAME record_dissent that bee cells dissent routes to (verbs/cells/dissent.rs) against opts.cell_id, and stamp dissent_recorded: true on success. A missing cell id or a refusal from the writer stamps dissent_recorded: false plus dissent_error naming the reason, and the raw dissent still rides the envelope. Never swallow it. The run's exit code is unchanged.

truths: The rendered brief names no bee command anywhere — the retargeted pin proves it.
The brief's result schema names the dissent fields, so a bee-ignorant worker can fill them without running anything.
A result carrying no dissent parses and re-emits with today's exact key set.
A malformed or partial dissent object parses as absent and never fails the round.
The severity is passed through unvalidated by the parser; the closed set is checked by record_dissent alone.
A carried dissent is written through record_dissent — the same function the CLI verb calls — so the record shape, secret scan, blocker tooth and claim release have one implementation.
A successful transcription stamps dissent_recorded: true in the emitted JSON envelope.
No cell id, or a writer refusal, stamps dissent_recorded: false plus dissent_error, and the raw dissent still rides the envelope.
The retarget of the mailbox.rs negative pin was proven red-first.

acceptance: A herding worker can hand back a dissent as data on the result file, the run verb records it through the one dissent writer, and the outcome of that write is visible in the envelope; the herding suite is green.
